title: Lighthouse client metrics playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, operational playbook for Customer Success (CS) preparing quarterly account reviews (QBRs) focused on production inference economics and reliability. Intended audience: CS managers, solutions engineers, and account owners. Use this as a reproducible checklist + metric definition reference when building SLI/SLO narratives for customers in Hosted, Dedicated, or Private modes.

Quick guidance (TL;DR):
- Metric definitions below are the canonical formulas we use internally for QBR tables.
- Use a 28-day rolling window for trend signals, but show 7/28/90 day snapshots during QBR.
- Highlight regressions at P95 or higher and cost anomalies when cost/token deviates >20% month-over-month.

Metric definitions (canonical):
1) Latency (generation):
   - Primary SLIs: P50_latency_ms, P95_latency_ms, P99_latency_ms
   - Definition: measured server-side from request-receive to final-token-send (includes batching wait + model kernel time). Exclude client-side network variance unless customer requests end-to-end.
   - Measurement window: sample all completed generation requests. For chat-style sessions include only full-response completions (no mid-stream aborts).
   - Formula notes: compute percentile over per-request durations in milliseconds. For batched requests compute per-request latency (time from request enqueue to response complete).

2) Uptime (availability):
   - Primary SLI: successful_requests_pct (SLA-focused)
   - Definition: percentage of requests that returned 2xx HTTP within configured timeout (default 30s). Exclude planned maintenance windows and intentional throttling events with customer notice.
   - Calculation: (successful_requests / attempted_requests) * 100 over a rolling 28d window.
   - SLO mapping example: SLO 99.9% for Dedicated gold; Hosted free-tier SLO is unconstrained but CS should call out regressions.

3) Cost per token (economics):
   - SLO-ish metric: cost_per_token_usd (observability only; not a contractual SLA)
   - Definition: amortized cost of compute + infra per generated token including overheads and caching effect.
   - Simplified formula we display in QBRs:
       cost_per_token = (compute_hourly_cost * hours_used / tokens_generated) + storage_and_network_allocated_per_token
   - Practical calculation (how we report): use model-run cost from runtime billing (USD) divided by tokens_output in that period, then apply cache-adjusted factor:
       effective_cost_per_token = runtime_cost_usd / (tokens_output * (1 - miss_rate))
     where miss_rate = fraction of requests that bypass cache (0.0 - 1.0).
   - Note: for customers using KV/prefix caching, annotate cost splits between cold vs warm generation.

4) Cache hit rate (workload caching):
   - Metric: cache_hit_pct and cache_miss_cost_delta
   - Definition: cache_hit_pct = cached_served_requests / cacheable_request_candidates * 100
   - Distinguish cache types: prefix cache (prompt-level), KV cache (inference attention/kvcache reuse), and app-layer (customer-side) caches. In QBRs, we focus on runtime prefix and KV cache hit rates because those directly reduce per-token compute.
   - Operational note: small increases in cache_hit_pct -> nonlinear savings depending on batch efficiency; translate to tokens_saved and USD savings in QBR narrative.

Measurement and telemetry sources:
- Primary source: runtime trace logs + telemetry (tag requests with model_version, route, customer_id, cache_status, batch_id).
- Fallback: per-invoice runtime cost buckets + token counters from usage pipeline.
- Cross-check: Redwood Console per-route dashboards (use date filters).
- Ownership: eng-observability maintains canonical queries; CS uses derived dashboards in Confluence link in linked_artifacts.

KPI table template (copy this verbatim into slides or email):
Columns (CSV-friendly): customer, tier, reporting_window, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, uptime_pct, cache_hit_pct, effective_cost_per_token_usd, trend_notes
Sample rows (fictional numbers):
RedwoodCo, enterprise, 28d, 120, 360, 820, 99.95, 42.7, 0.0031, "P95 improved after kernel patch; cache tuning planned"
AcmeOps, growth, 28d, 210, 720, 1500, 99.80, 18.2, 0.0075, "High tail due to occasional large-batch bursts; recommend batching cap"
Startable, self-serve, 28d, 95, 240, 600, 99.60, 6.1, 0.0120, "Low cache usage; enable prefix caching on common prompts"

How to interpret / narrative guidance for CS: 
- Latency: Surface P95 first. If P95 regresses by >25% vs prior 28d, call SRE + solutions to confirm kernel/regression or traffic pattern change.
- Uptime: If uptime drops below customer SLO threshold, open a post-incident note and include runbook ID.
- Cost/token: Show effective_cost_per_token and compare to peers in same tier; highlight quantized policy changes (int8/4-bit) separately.
- Cache: Translate cache_hit_pct into tokens saved and USD saved for the period; use a simple multiplier to convert (tokens_saved * effective_cost_per_token).

QBR slide / talking points checklist (short):
- One-liner summary (health + econ): example: "Stable latency (P95 360ms), 99.95% uptime, cost/token improved 12% QoQ due to cache tuning."
- Top 3 signals (with hyperlinks): latency regressions, cost anomalies, cache opportunities.
- Actions: 1) recommended runtime config changes (e.g., lower batching window for low-latency routes), 2) rollout plan for prefix cache on top 5 prompts, 3) ops follow-up and owner.
- Risks & mitigations: capacity constraints, model-compat regressions, high-variance tail for multimodal loads.

Operations checklist for CS before QBR:
- Pull 7/28/90 day SLI snapshots from Console and paste into table.
- Run "cache-savings projection" script (link in linked_artifacts) and attach CSV to QBR packet.
- Confirm last 3 deploys and model rollouts; note any canary or fallback events.
- Attach trending graphs for Cost per token and P95 latency.

Open questions & TODOs (for internal follow-up):
- Decide canonical handling for client-observed network latency: show internal-server-only by default, add an "end-to-end" optional column? (Owner: Jordan)
- Create small template script for converting cache_hits -> USD savings and store in Confluence (Owner: Priya).
- Add a short glossary slide that explains amortization assumptions behind cost_per_token (Owner: Ethan).

References and quick links:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood/cs/lighthouse-metrics
- Observability tickets: JIRA-OBS-210, JIRA-OBS-211 (kernel perf investigations)
- Internal PR with cost calc: https://github.com/redwood-inference/pr/2145

Notes to self / CS handoff language (two-line):
- "We've seen stable baseline latency this quarter but caching is uneven across the account. If they enable prefix caching for their top-10 prompts we project ~25% lower monthly bill for generation.
- Next steps: schedule a 30-minute tech-check with solutions engineering to scope prefix cache rollout and batching policy tweaks."

End.
